information.title: Information
information.description: The settings for the basic information of an element (ID, name, explanation, icon, and colour)

points: These are the basic information fields shared by every element in a world (a category, an action, an item, a group, an event, a skill, and a preset).
You set them individually for each element.

options.infoText: The version number of the world

points: Enter a number of `0` or more (a whole number or a decimal). The default value is `0`.
Generally the whole-number part represents the major version and the decimal part the minor version.
The version of the development (development) is the version of the editor, so it is a different thing.

options.infoText: The name of the author of the world

points: Enter a handle name or a nickname.
It must be from 3 to 20 characters, and only single-byte letters and digits, spaces and `!` `?` `.` `,` `-` can be used.

options.infoText: The URL of the website of the author

points: If you have your own homepage or social media, enter its URL.
The player can check this URL through the link.
If there is none, leave it blank. The initial value is `https://`.

options.infoText: The URL of the game

points: Enter the URL where the game of this world is placed.
Enter the URL of a top page such as index.html, including the domain.
It is a field for recording where the world was placed. When the place to put it is not decided, leave it blank.
A published world works as a PWA. A PWA is a feature that lets it be installed and work like an app you can play offline as well.
The settings of the PWA are made with relative paths, so it works as it is wherever it is placed, regardless of the value of this field.

options.infoText: The rough time until the world is played through
The number of the playing time

points: Set it as a whole number of `1` or more. The default value is `1`.

options.infoText: The unit of time (hours, minutes and so on)

points: Choose from seconds, minutes, hours, days, years, centuries and infinite. The default value is days.
Infinite is used for a world with no end.
It is the estimated playing time needed to complete playing the world.
It can be checked as a guide when the player plays.
It is only a reference time, and there is no clear definition of what counts as completing the world.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: The basic information of the world and the information of the author

points: They are the fields that explain the content of the world.
Set them so that they are easy to understand when a user chooses the world.
Apart from the URL, these settings have no effect on the progress of the game.

options.infoText: Details
The time limit on the offline progress

points: Sets how many hours at most the progress while offline runs for.

For example, when you set 6 hours, the process of returning from offline is handled up to 6 hours, and even when you return from offline after a longer time away, the offline time is treated as 6 hours.
When you set 0 hours, no process at all is handled on returning from offline.
The maximum value is 24 hours.

options.infoText: The level cap of each category

points: Sets the cap on the level of each category. The default value is `100`.
Even when experience is gained, the level stops at this value and the excess is discarded. The same applies when a reward adds levels directly.
When the level in the save data is over the cap, it is trimmed down to the cap on loading.
The level bar and the progress rate in the statistics are shown with this value as the denominator.
A category whose numeric is disabled does not gain levels, so this value is not related to it.

options.infoText: Requiring the level of the category of the attribute in order to execute an action

points: When it is enabled, the requirement "the level of the category of the attribute is at or above the level of that action" is added automatically at the head of the requirements of each action.
When no attribute is set, the category it belongs to is used.
When the numeric of the category of the attribute is disabled, it does not gain levels, so nothing is added.
The added requirement is written in when the world is loaded, so it is shown on the screen of the player just like an ordinary requirement.

options.infoText: How many times the properties become for every 10 of level gap

points: Sets how many times the properties become for every `10` that the gap between the level of the category and the level of the action widens. The default value is `1.5`, and a value below `1` cannot be set.
The multiplier is calculated as (property ratio)^(level gap÷10). When the level gap is `0` it is `1` times, and the value set on the action is used as it is.
Attack and experience increase by this multiplier, and defence (the damage taken) and speed (the required time) decrease by the same multiplier.

Accuracy, evasion, success rate, and the amount of recovery are values that stay within `0` to `100`%, so the multiplier applies to the ratio between the side that comes about and the side that does not. `0`% and `100`% do not change, and a value in between never goes over `100`%.

For defence, evasion, and speed the multiplier works at half strength (a level gap of `20` amounts to a level gap of `10` for the other properties). Defence and evasion apply twice over, to the rate of being hit and to the damage taken, and speed applies to all the other properties as the number of executions, so their effect is weakened to keep the balance.
A guide is (the experience growth rate) to the power of `6.7`. Above it, levelling up accelerates as the level rises, and below it, levelling up in the later stages takes more time.
Setting it to `1` removes the influence of the level gap. Making the value larger makes the advantage and the disadvantage from the level gap steeper.

options.infoText: The increasing rate of the difficulty of levelling up

points: It is the growth rate of the experience needed to reach the next level as the level of a category rises. The default value is `1.05`, and a value below `1` cannot be set.
Making this value larger raises the difficulty. Setting it to `1` keeps the experience needed the same at every level.
The experience needed to reach the next level is (experience growth rate)^(current level-1). Levels are counted with the decimals discarded.
The experience gained after the cap (the maximum category level) is reached is discarded.

options.infoText: The language in which you create the world

points: Sets which language you are writing the name and the description of the world in. It is the language that the translations are based on.
It is also the language shown first when a player starts the game.
When translations is disabled, the player cannot switch away from this language.
It is a separate setting from the display language of the world editor itself. You choose the display language of the editor when you open the editor.

options.infoText: Whether to prepare translations for multiple languages

points: When it is enabled, players can switch to whichever language they like and play in it.
When it is disabled, it is fixed to the language chosen in language, and the switching operation itself is not available.
When you enable it, you need to prepare the translation data for each language. The published package includes the translation data.
What switches are the names and the descriptions defined in the world. The translations of the common wording of the screen (the presets) are always included regardless of this setting.

options.infoText: The settings of the currency (coins) used in the game

points: Sets the currency used in the game. At least one is required.
You can define several currencies, and you set each of them as information (ID, name, icon, colour, and so on).
Currencies are used for buying and selling items and for expanding the capacity and the queue.

The first currency is treated as the main currency, and it is used when no currency ID (`coinId`) is specified for an item, the capacity, or the queue, or when an ID that is not in the list of currencies is specified.
A currency is treated as a kind of item. In requirements and rewards, refer to the ID set here as an item. It does not belong to a category, and it is not subject to equipping or trading.

information.title: Capacity Information
information.description: The ID, name, icon, and colour for treating the capacity as an item

points: These are the basic information fields shared by every element in a world (a category, an action, an item, a group, an event, a skill, and a preset).
You set them individually for each element.

options.infoText: The initial inventory capacity (the number of kinds of items that can be held)

points: It is the initial capacity at the start of the game (the number of kinds of items that can be held). The default value is `10`.
Setting it to `0` makes the capacity unlimited, and at the same time buying capacity becomes unavailable.

options.infoText: The initial price for increasing the capacity by one

points: It is the base price (in coins) for increasing the inventory capacity by one slot. Set it as an integer of `1` or more.
The actual price is calculated as "base price × increasing rate^number of purchases made".
For example, with a base price of 100 and an increasing rate of 1.2, the first time is 100 coins, the second time 120 coins, and the third time 144 coins.

options.infoText: The increasing rate of the cost of expanding the capacity

points: It is the multiplier for how much the cost of expanding the capacity increases at the nth purchase. The default value is `1.2`.
With `1.0` the price is always the same, and with `1.2` it becomes 20% more expensive with every purchase.
Formula: base price × increasing rate^number of purchases made

options.infoText: The ID of the currency used for expanding the capacity

points: Specifies the ID of the currency (coins) used for the expansion price of the inventory capacity.
When it is left blank, or when an ID that is not in the list of currencies is specified, the main currency (the first of coins) is used.

options.infoText: The maximum number of times the capacity can be bought

points: It is the cap on the number of times the capacity can be bought with a currency.
Setting it to `0` allows unlimited purchases.
Setting it to `-1` makes it impossible to buy.
An increase of the capacity by a reward is not subject to this cap.
Manages the cap on the number of kinds of items a player can hold.
It is managed by the number of kinds of items held, not by the number owned of each item.
Setting `initialCount` to 0 makes the capacity unlimited, and buying capacity also becomes unavailable.
When you refer to the capacity item in requirements or rewards, use the ID set here or `capacity`.

information.title: Queue Information
information.description: The ID, name, icon, and colour for treating the queue as an item

points: These are the basic information fields shared by every element in a world (a category, an action, an item, a group, an event, a skill, and a preset).
You set them individually for each element.

options.infoText: The number of slots for successive execution at the start of the game

points: It is the number of slots in the queue at the start of the game. The default value is `1`.
The minimum value is `1` (because the one being executed uses one slot; there is no `0` = unlimited handling as there is for the capacity).

options.infoText: The initial price for increasing the slots by one

points: It is the base price (in coins) for increasing the slots for successive execution by one. Set it as an integer of `1` or more.
The actual price is calculated as "base price × increasing rate^number of purchases made".
For example, with a base price of 100 and an increasing rate of 1.2, the first time is 100 coins, the second time 120 coins, and the third time 144 coins.

options.infoText: The increasing rate of the cost of expanding the slots

points: It is the multiplier for how much the cost of expanding the slots increases at the nth purchase. The default value is `1.2`.
With `1.0` the price is always the same, and with `1.2` it becomes 20% more expensive with every purchase.
Formula: base price × increasing rate^number of purchases made
The way it increases is the same as the increasing rate of the capacity. For a guide to the multiplier, see the table for the capacity.

options.infoText: The ID of the currency used for expanding the slots

points: Specifies the ID of the currency (coins) used for the expansion price of the slots for successive execution.
When it is left blank, or when an ID that is not in the list of currencies is specified, the main currency (the first of coins) is used.

options.infoText: The maximum number of times the slots can be bought

points: It is the cap on the number of times the slots for successive execution can be bought with a currency.
Setting it to `0` allows unlimited purchases.
Setting it to `-1` makes it impossible to buy.
An increase of the slots by a reward is not subject to this cap.
Manages the number of slots in the queue for executing actions in succession.
The queue includes the action being executed, and the action at its head is the one executed. When the slots are `1`, there is only the one being executed and no waiting can be held.
As with the capacity, the number of slots can be bought with a currency, and it can also be increased by specifying the queue item as a reward of an action or an event.
When you refer to the queue item in requirements or rewards, use the ID set here or `queue`.

options.infoText: Details
The level gap correction to the stamina damage dealt to the opponent

points: The higher the value on the player side, the more damage is dealt to the opponent.
A value set on an action or on a skill of the opponent becomes the attack of the opponent side, and the higher it is, the more damage the player takes.

options.infoText: The level gap correction to the stamina damage taken from the opponent

points: The higher the value on the player side, the more the damage taken is reduced.
A value set on an action or on a skill of the opponent becomes the defence of the opponent side, and the higher it is, the less damage the player deals.

options.infoText: The level gap correction to the miss rate of the attack

points: The higher the value on the player side, the lower the miss rate of the attack.
A value set on an action or on a skill of the opponent becomes the accuracy of the opponent side, and the higher it is, the harder it is for the player to evade the attack of the opponent.

options.infoText: The level gap correction to the rate of evading the attack of the opponent

points: The higher the value on the player side, the easier it is to evade the attack of the opponent.
A value set on an action or on a skill of the opponent becomes the evasion of the opponent side, and the higher it is, the harder it is for the attack of the player to land.

defaultCombat.title: Combat Values
defaultCombat.description: The default combat parameters common to all actions

points: They are the basic combat corrections on the player side, applied in common to all actions of the `stamina` type.
The combat values (property) of each action are the values on the opponent side, so they work in the direction of cancelling out the values set here.

general.title: General
general.description: Basic game settings such as the language and the level settings

options.infoText: Details
The colour that becomes the background of the bar

points: It is used as the background colour of the bar.
Because it is also the colour that becomes the base of the whole screen, the colour of the selected row is made from this colour too.
The swatches of elements with no colour set and the background of the toasts become the middle colour between this colour and the text colour.

options.infoText: The colour of the text and the background

points: It is used as the colour of the text.
The gradient of the background is also made from this colour. When a background image is set, the same gradient is thinned and laid over the image.

Taking a large difference in brightness from the bar colour makes the text easier to read. In a world where the difference is small, the swatches of elements with no colour set also become harder to tell apart.

options.infoText: The colour of the shadow of the bar

points: It is used as the colour of the shadow cast on the bars and the header.
Making it a darker colour than the bar colour gives a natural shadow.

options.infoText: The background image of the whole game

points: It sets the background image of the game.
When no image is set, the background becomes a gradient based on the text colour.
The image is automatically reduced so that it fits within 256×256 pixels. GIF and AVIF are converted to PNG.
When a background image is set on a category, the image on the category side takes priority on the screen of that category.
The image you set can be deleted with the Delete Image button.

design.title: Design
design.description: The look settings of the world, such as the colours and the font

points: They are the settings about the display of the world.

The two colours decided here (the bar colour and the text colour) become the base of the whole screen, and every colour used on the screen, such as the selected row, the heading of a group and the colours of affirmation and negation, is made from them.
The background image alone can be swapped per category, and in that case the setting on the category side takes priority.

options.infoText: Details
The build version number of the editor

points: The version number of the editor at the moment the new world was created is recorded automatically.
It is not updated even when an existing world is loaded and edited.
The developer cannot change this content.

options.infoText: The memo record for the developer

points: The developer can write it freely as a memo.
It has no relation to publishing the game.

options.infoText: The error record of the validation result

points: The result of validating the world is saved here automatically.
For example, it shows as errors things such as a kind of character that cannot be entered, or a number entered over the upper limit.
When there was not a single error, a message showing success is saved instead, on just one line.
The developer cannot change this content.
While errors remain, the world cannot be published. When you operate publish, the validation runs first and stops there if there are errors.

options.infoText: The time the world was first created

points: It is the date and time when the world was first created.

options.infoText: The time the last save was performed

points: It is the date and time when the world was last saved.

options.infoText: The time the last publish was performed

points: It is the date and time when the world was last published.

options.infoText: The record of the creation, the saving and the publishing

points: The times of the creation, the saving and the publishing of the world are recorded automatically.
The developer cannot change this content.

options.infoText: Whether the auto save feature is enabled or disabled

points: It shows whether the content of the editing is saved to the browser automatically.
You cannot rewrite this field directly. You change it with the auto save toggle in the menu of the editor.

development.title: Development
development.description: The management of the memos and the errors while the world is developed

points: It is used while the world is developed.
It concerns the development and the testing of this world and has no effect on what is played.
The player never sees what relates to the development.

options.infoText: The display group classification of the category

points: Apply one of those defined in the groups directly under the world.

enum_titles: Secreted: Completely hidden from all UI (not even as a hint) until all requirements are met
Hidden: Fully concealed (grayed out, no name) until referenced or conditions met
Hinted: Name shown as a teaser but not operable until released (default)
Released: Unlocked and operable from the start regardless of conditions
options.infoText: The initial display and unlock state of the element (it moves up to a higher state automatically once the firing requirements are met)

points: secreted: It does not appear in the UI at all until every requirement is met (it does not show up in the hints either, and it is masked in the lists of requirements and rewards as well).
hidden: While it is referred to by none of the unlocked elements and its requirements are unmet, it is hidden completely (the name is greyed out and it cannot be operated).
hinted (the default): Only the name is shown in advance, but it cannot be operated until it is unlocked.
released: It is unlocked and can be operated from the start regardless of the conditions (formerly "shown from the start").

options.infoText: The kind of element referred to as the condition
The ID of the element referred to as the condition

points: Set the ID of the category, action, or item referred to as the condition.
When group totalling (requiringGroup) is enabled on an event, it is treated as the ID of a group rather than of an individual element.

options.infoText: The number the condition needs

points: The condition is met when it is at or above the value you specify.
Set it as an integer of 0 or more. The default value is `1`.

options.infoText: The chance that the item is consumed (0 to 1, works only when the type is an item)

The level gap correction to the stamina damage dealt to the opponent

points: The higher the value on the player side, the more damage is dealt to the opponent.
A value set on an action or on a skill of the opponent becomes the attack of the opponent side, and the higher it is, the more damage the player takes.

points: The higher the value on the player side, the lower the miss rate of the attack.

property.title: Combat Values
property.description: The settings for the combat corrections on actions of the stamina type

points: These are corrections that work only on actions of the `stamina` type.
Each value is calculated as an extra correction to the level gap between the player and the action.

For example, when the attack value is 10, the attack damage is calculated as if the level of the player were 10 higher than the level of the action. A negative value is a correction in the opposite direction.
Depending on where you set it, the value belongs either to the player side or to the opponent side.

A value on the opponent side works so as to cancel out the field opposite to it. The defence of the opponent cancels out the attack of the player, the attack of the opponent cancels out the defence of the player, the evasion of the opponent cancels out the accuracy of the player, and the accuracy of the opponent cancels out the evasion of the player.
Recovery alone cancels out against the same field, and the higher the recovery of the opponent, the less the player recovers.

properties.title: Property
properties.description: The property effects the item has

points: These are the effect fields you can set on an item.

An item whose equipment type is `necessary` or `consumable` applies its effect only while it is equipped. `unnecessary` applies its effect just by being owned, and the size of the effect is proportional to the number owned (twice as much if you own two).

Because the number owned is itself the multiplier of an `unnecessary` effect, `maximum` (the maximum number owned) becomes the ceiling of the effect. When you balance it, set it together with `maximum`.
The value of every field is calculated as something that adjusts the level gap between the level of the player and the level of the action.
For example, when the attack value is 10, the attack is calculated as if the level of the player were 10 higher than the level of the action. A negative value works the other way around.
How much the level gap matters is decided by `propertyRatio` in general (2 by default), and it changes by that multiplier for every 10 of level gap.
When `numeric` of the category is disabled, the real level gap is treated as 0, so the value you set here becomes the level gap as it is.
A field that works by division, such as the required time and the damage taken, tops out at 100 times (down to one hundredth for the required time).
For an item that has to be equipped, only the one equipped in each equipment group takes effect.
An item whose owned count is 0 produces no effect, whatever its equipment type.
attack, defence, accuracy, evasion, and restore work only on actions of the `stamina` type.

When an ID that does not exist is specified, it is ignored.

items.description: Elements for goods such as equipment and consumables

points: It is a special effect that is drawn each turn and fires in a combat (`stamina`) action. It does not fire in an action of any other type.

options.infoText: Details
The kind of element referred to as the condition
The ID of the element referred to as the condition

points: Set the ID of the category, action, or item referred to as the condition.
When group totalling (requiringGroup) is enabled on an event, it is treated as the ID of a group rather than of an individual element.

options.infoText: The number the condition needs

points: The condition is met when it is at or above the value you specify.
Set it as an integer of 0 or more. The default value is `1`.

options.infoText: The chance that the item is consumed (0 to 1, works only when the type is an item)

points: This is the chance of consuming the item when the conditions are met and the action is performed.
`1` always consumes it, `0.5` consumes it with a 50% chance, and `0` does not consume it.

The default value is `1` (always consumed). On the conditions of an event (a task, a changed event, or a fixed event), however, the default value is `0` (not consumed) so that what you hold does not decrease when you achieve it.

With `0` the stock is not reduced, so you can perform the action as many times as you like as long as the number owned reaches the value of the condition. Use it when you want the condition to be only that the item is equipped.
It does not work when the type is anything other than an item.

options.infoText: Whether the item has to be equipped for the condition (works only when the type is an item)

points: When it is enabled, the condition needs the item not only to be owned but also to be equipped.
Whether it is equipped is judged by the equipment of the category the item belongs to.
It does not work when the type is anything other than an item.

requirements.title: Requirement（On Completion）
requirements.description: The conditions for obtaining the reward

points: These are the conditions you set on each element: a category, an action, an item, and an event.
Unless every condition you set is met, the operation shown in the table cannot be done.
Depending on the unlock setting (unlocked) of the element, the element itself is not shown on the screen until the conditions are met.

options.infoText: Treats the id in the conditions as a group ID and judges by the total value of the elements that belong to it

points: When it is enabled, the id you set in the conditions (requirements) is treated as the ID of a group directly under the world.
A condition whose type is a category is judged by the total level of every category that belongs to that group.
A condition whose type is an action is judged by the total number of times every action that belongs to that group has been performed.
A condition whose type is an item is judged by the total number owned of every item that belongs to that group.
An element that is not unlocked (anything other than released) is not included in the total.
The consumption chance (chance) and the equipment condition (equipment) of an item are ignored, and the number owned is never consumed. They are used only for the judgement.
When it is disabled, the id in the conditions is treated as the ID of an individual category, action or item, as before.

options.infoText: Details
The kind of element that is gained
The ID that identifies the element to gain
The number that is gained

points: Setting a negative value decreases the number owned, the number of times performed, or the level. It never goes below 0, though.
When a maximum owned count (maximum) is set on the item, the number owned does not grow beyond that value.

When the type is a category, the value you set is added to the level as it is (1 for one level). The usual way is to adjust it with the experience setting of the action. Unless you have a special purpose, this setting is not needed.
The level of a category never goes below 0, and it never goes over `maxCategoryLevels` in general (the maximum level of a category).
Set the value as an integer.

options.infoText: The chance that the gain succeeds (a negative value is evaluated only on failure)

points: Set the chance of gaining it as a decimal from -1 to 1. The absolute value is used to judge the chance.
When the value is positive it is evaluated only when the action succeeds: `1` always gains it, and `0.5` gains it with a 50% chance.
When the value is negative it is evaluated only when the action fails: `-1` always gains it, and `-0.5` gains it with a 50% chance.
With `0` it is gained neither on success nor on failure.
The default value is `1` (always gained on success).

With Iconify you can set an emoji that does not depend on the environment

options.infoText: Using the Iconify icon sets

points: This is the icon that represents the element.
When you have set an image, that is shown with priority.

options.infoText: Using any image file you like

points: This is the image that represents the element.
When it is taken in, it is automatically shrunk to within 60x60 pixels and compressed again.
It is not needed when you have set Iconify or an emoji.
For the icon you can set an image, Iconify, or an emoji.
Iconify is a service that provides icons of many kinds.
When you set more than one of these, they are shown in the order of priority of image, Iconify, and emoji.

options.infoText: The setting for the colour the element is shown in

points: As the colour of the element, it applies to the icon of the element and to its background colour.
You choose it from the colour picker of the editor.
Black (`#000000`) is treated as the value that means "no colour is set". The initial value of the colour picker is this black as well.
When you want it to look black, specify a colour shifted slightly, such as `#010101`.

unique.title: Fixed Event
unique.description: The messages and rewards that activate at set moments

points: It activates at set moments, such as when the world is opened for the first time or when a game over occurs, and opens a dedicated screen.
One is prepared for each moment, and none can be added or deleted. Leave the moments you do not use blank.
They are not shown in the missions or in the task list. Set what becomes achieved when its requirements are met with a task.
When the moment comes about, the event activates and opens a dedicated screen to show its content.

The reward is obtained automatically at the same time as the activation. There is no claiming operation and no ribbon as there is for a task, and the cap on the kinds of items that can be held is not checked either.
When requirements are set, the reward is obtained only when those requirements were met at the time of activation. When none are set, it is obtained on every activation.
The requirements are only looked at to see whether they are met, so items are not reduced even when a consumption chance is set.

On activation you can change the level of a category, the number of executions of an action, and the number of items held. By setting a minus quantity, you can also use it in ways such as making the player lose their belongings on a game over.
When you leave the name, the description, and the icon blank, the default wording and icon built into the player are used.

events.title: Event
events.description: All the events of the world, gathering the tasks, the changed events, and the fixed events

points: The events of a world are made up of three kinds: tasks, changed events (changed), and fixed events (unique).
A task is a mission that becomes achieved when its requirements are met.
A changed event is an event for internal processing, not shown on the screen, that activates repeatedly with an increase in a quantity as its trigger.
A fixed event is a slot prepared one per moment, which cannot be added or deleted.

presets.title: Preset
presets.description: Customising how the system elements are shown

points: Replaces the UI text and the icons built into the game engine (the player) in advance.

Only those whose ID matches an existing preset are replaced. Adding a preset whose ID does not match an existing one is not an error, but it has no effect on the display because there is nothing that refers to it.
Only the fields you set are replaced. If you set only the icon, for example, the original ones are used for the name, the colour and every other field.
Overwriting the name and the explanation takes priority over the translations for each language built into the player. The string you overwrite is shown in that very form in every language.
When you want to change the wording for each language, specify it in the translation file `translations/world` that is output once translation is enabled. That one takes the highest priority.
